title: Review of the test pages
subtitle: Two of the test pages are judged: the one made with faults and the one made without.
note: The pages are made to test the measurement. The faults on the page with faults are there on purpose.
summary: The page with faults cannot be used on a phone. The calm page works, but is flat to look at.

faults.title: The page with faults
faults.job: Get the user to sign up with their email address.

layer1.note: The page has two h1s and five sections that have nothing to do with each other. The form is more than two screen heights down.
The most important thing is at the bottom, and everything at the top is centred and the same size.
The button only says “Send”, and the field only has a placeholder.
The field has no label, blocks paste and is 30 px tall with 13 px text (`test/pages/faults.html:21`).
After an error the page comes back without a message and with an empty field (`test/server.mjs:75`).
The button looks the same before, during and after a press.
No menu and no main landmark. The only link is 14 px tall.
The page scrolls sideways at 390 px, and zoom is disabled.
Light grey text on white (2.05:1), a link without a focus ring and a button that cannot be reached by keyboard.
The page looks like a collection of parts, not one page.

layer3.note: Arial carries all the text. One paragraph has a line height of 1.05, and another is 10 px tall.
A paragraph sits 3 px to the right of its heading. Field and button are 30 and 36 px tall.
Cards inside cards, and frosted glass on three surfaces that do not lie on top of anything.
Purple gradient with a glow, and grey text on top of the coloured surface.
The send button has neither a hover nor a pressed state.
`transition: all`, a width that is animated, a curve that bounces, and a spinner that keeps running under “reduce motion”.
The button does not respond to a press.
Inner corners of 16 px inside a frame with 8 px (`test/pages/faults.html:80`).

good: The email field has `type="email"`, so the phone shows the right keyboard.

life.values: `scale(.97)` over 120 ms with `cubic-bezier(.23,1,.32,1)`, and a shade darker

faults.dontAnimate: The headings and the error message. They must be readable at once.

clean.title: The calm page
clean.job: Get the user to sign up with their email address.

layer1.note: The menu has one link, and it points to the page itself.
axe finds no errors, and focus can be seen. The page has not been tried with a screen reader.

layer3.note: The page is completely flat. Nothing sets the form apart from the text around it.
The button's text changes to “Sending …” in one jump.

good: The button says what happens: “Send me a link”. It locks after the first press.
The error sits next to the field, and what was typed stays.
Field and button are 48 px tall with 18 px text.

aiLook.answer: Yes, for the page with faults. The purple gradient, the three matching cards and the centred text say nothing about what the page is for. No, for the calm page.
findings: The three cards “Fast”, “Secure” and “Simple” could be on any page at all.

customer.task: Sign up with your email address on the page with faults
customer.conclusion: The form came back empty without saying why.

steps.step: Opened the page on a phone
steps.saw: A purple heading, three cards and a lot of text
A small field with the text “Your email”

steps.step: Typed an address without a domain and pressed Send
steps.saw: The same page with an empty field
steps.thought: Was it sent? I do not know.

stumbled: The form is more than two screen heights down, and nothing at the top points down to it.
After the error the field is empty, and the page does not say what was wrong.

notSeen.page: The receipt after a valid address
notSeen.why: The test server always answers with an error.

limits: Only two of the pages are judged in layers 1 and 3. The rest are only measured.
